summary: Randolph County places its defined server-based data processing facility use in HI-CD (Heavy Industrial Conditional District). This is conditional district zoning, not by-right industrial use.
locator: Art. 600 §621, Data Processing Facility, PDF p. 207

summary: Outdoor equipment must be at least 1,000 feet from existing residences and listed sensitive uses, including schools, daycares, churches, hospitals, camps, parks and community or recreation centers.

A licensed professional engineer must certify the proposed closed-loop water or liquid cooling system will minimize water use. For liquid cooling, the certification must identify daily usage and the water source.
evidence: closed-loop water or a liquid cooling system

summary: The facility must connect to the existing grid before final occupancy certification. On-site generation is limited to grid emergencies and routine testing totaling at most four hours per month.
evidence: routine testing up to four hours a month

summary: In county zoning jurisdiction, installation, construction and modifications beyond routine maintenance require both a conditional use permit and county building permit. The section names only Heavy Industrial (H-I) and Agricultural Preservation (AG-P) and references a petition.

The default separation from listed sensitive properties is one mile measured property line to property line. A stamped design showing noise below 75 dBA at the nearest data-center property line may support a reduction, never below half a mile. A written waiver in this range entails a noise mitigation plan.

Before a grid-connected facility can receive a permit, its operator must provide utility approval and verification of available capacity, adequately sized infrastructure and no interference or voltage fluctuations. The requirement exempts off-grid systems.

Springdale classifies an electronic data storage center under Office. Its definition expressly covers the operation of computer hardware and equipment that processes, stores or routes electronic data. This row does not infer district permission for every office or every type of data center.
locator: Zoning Ordinance, commercial use types, paragraph U (Office), PDF p. 113
evidence: Also includes electronic data storage centers

summary: For large-scale data processing facilities as defined, all equipment and structures must be at least 50 feet from the site-plan facility boundary and 1,320 feet from any church, school or residence. Maximum height is 35 feet, excluding transmission lines and utility poles.

The large-scale facility application requires a narrative, layout showing churches, schools or homes within a quarter-mile of the perimeter, an acoustic-engineering study and owner/operator signatures. The county may request other reasonably necessary documentation.
evidence: A study prepared by an acoustical engineer

summary: The village lists qualifying data processing facilities by right in Commercial (C) and Light Industrial & Warehousing (LIW). Its definition covers digital records managed using a mainframe and excludes general offices, computer sales and personal/business services.
locator: Zoning Ordinance §§3.7.2, 3.8.2 and 14.6, PDF pp. 65, 69 and 180

summary: The use tables for Commercial and Light Industrial & Warehousing specify a parking maximum of four spaces per 1,000 square feet for a data processing facility.
locator: Zoning Ordinance §§3.7.2 and 3.8.2, MAXIMUM PARKING column, PDF pp. 65, 69

summary: Facilities that house systems used to store, process or distribute data remotely are allowed only in Saluda’s C-3 Commercial district, with a special use permit.
locator: Zoning Ordinance, C-3 use-specific requirements, (2)(B), PDF p. 43; definition p. 87

summary: The application must include a project narrative, a site plan locating equipment, access and screening, and an acoustical engineer’s study of anticipated sound and mitigation.
evidence: A study prepared by an acoustical engineer

summary: Before installing a grid-connected system, the operator must supply evidence that the utility approved the installation. The requirement exempts off-grid systems.
